page.title: Reader — Turn saved sources into working knowledge
page.description: A personal research library for articles and PDFs.

hero.title: Turn the things you save into *things you can use.*
hero.lede: Reader is for people who save serious articles and PDFs, then lose them among browser tabs and bookmarks. It gives each source a quiet place to read, mark, question, and find again.
hero.note: Browser-local start · Google sign-in for the library · No checkout

hero.caption: Illustrative interface · example text, not a customer document

blocks.title: A saved tab is *only an intention.*
blocks.lede: Reader earns its place after “save”. It carries one source through attentive reading and back into reach when the thought becomes useful.

points.title: Capture the source
points.body: Paste an article URL or upload a PDF. Reader keeps the source and prepares it for focused reading.

points.title: Read without the page
points.body: Web clutter falls away. The text, document structure, reading controls and your place remain.

points.title: Mark what matters
points.body: Highlight the exact passage, leave a note beside it, or listen when reading is not practical.

points.title: Find the thought again
points.body: Search the library, return through tags and lists, arrange a board, or question the open source.

blocks.title: Keep the source, the mark, and *the next question* together.

points.title: Articles and PDFs, one shelf
points.body: Web articles and PDFs live in the same library. PDF text is extracted for search and source-grounded discussion.

points.title: More than one way back
points.body: Full-text search, tags, lists and boards give the same source several useful ways back in.

points.title: AI over what you chose
points.body: Summaries and chat work on material you opened. Use the Fleet gateway or browser-held keys.

blocks.title: Maintained for real use, *not expansion for its own sake.*
blocks.lede: Reader is a mature personal-use product in maintenance-first support. New work is limited to problems that block the capture-to-reading loop.

points.title: No account
points.body: Capture and read in this browser without a Reader account.

points.title: Google sign-in
points.body: Account library, isolated per user; PDFs behind an ownership-checking proxy.

points.title: Extension
points.body: Source-built MV3 companion for local unpacked installs.

points.title: Commerce
points.body: No public plan or checkout, and no promise either way.

items.q: Does Reader publish what I save?
items.a: No. Libraries are private by default. Sharing an article or board requires an explicit share action.
AI features work on the material you open and ask about. Browser-held keys are used per request and never stored server-side.

items.q: Can I install the Chrome extension?
items.a: It is available from source for local unpacked installation. Public browser-store distribution is deferred.

items.q: Can I take my data out?
items.a: Yes. Reader includes a JSON export for account-scoped articles, boards, and lists.

blocks.title: Bring one source you mean *to understand.*
blocks.lede: Start in this browser, or sign in with Google for the account-backed library.

footer.summary: A maintained personal research library for turning saved sources into working knowledge. Personal use, maintenance-first, no public checkout.
